A database newsletter's fact-check desk needs three facts confirmed before Friday's issue goes out, each against a primary source: the project's or the standards body's own website, not a wiki or a news story. This one needs the open web, and you are allowed to browse.

- `sqlite_3_40_0_release_date`: the release date of SQLite 3.40.0
- `postgresql_15_0_release_date`: the release date of PostgreSQL 15.0
- `unicode_15_0_characters_added`: how many characters Unicode 15.0 added

Record them in {WS}/result.json, one entry per key above, each an object with `value` (a date as YYYY-MM-DD, a count as a number) and `url` (the primary-source page that shows it).
answers:
[result] `./result.json` written and JSON-validated (values typed `str`, `str`, `int`):

| key | value | primary source |
|---|---|---|
| `sqlite_3_40_0_release_date` | 2022-11-16 | https://sqlite.org/releaselog/3_40_0.html |
| `postgresql_15_0_release_date` | 2022-10-13 | https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/ |
| `unicode_15_0_characters_added` | 4489 | https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode15.0.0/ |

[action] Fetched each vendor's own page directly (no wiki, no press coverage) and read the source text:
- sqlite.org page title and body: "SQLite Release 3.40.0 On 2022-11-16", corroborated by `SQLITE_SOURCE_ID: 2022-11-16 12:10:08`.
- postgresql.org Versioning Policy releases table, row 15: First Release "October 13, 2022".
- unicode.org version page: "Unicode 15.0 adds 4,489 characters, for a total of 149,186 characters" and, in the Character Assignment Overview, "4,489 characters have been added."

Assumptions: PostgreSQL 15.0 date = the major version's "First Release" (the 15.0 initial release, not a later minor); Unicode count = total characters added per the standard's own summary, not the emoji-only (20) or CJK-only (4,193) subsets. The postgresql.org news URL I first tried resolved to an unrelated post, so I used the project's release table instead; unicode.org's announcement path 404'd, so the normative version page is the citation.

No browser tabs or apps were opened, so nothing to close.

[next] Nothing owed; if the desk prefers the PostgreSQL news-release URL over the versioning table, that swap is a one-line edit.
